statusText: Tail risk low as NQ futures hold a 0.44% overnight band while the crude and long-end amplifiers retrace; mapped policy state EA_ON with elevated Stress.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 16 because the overnight advance remains a shallow 136.75-point drift that only partially retraces the prior session's 1.39% decline, price sits 38-44 points below the band high rather than holding an extreme, the 10-year has retraced to 5.23% from a 5.33% session high, and crude is down 0.8-1.1% after Washington ruled out an Iran strike before the 3 November midterms. Stress stays elevated at 57 on the unresolved AI revenue repricing, long-end yields near 24-year highs, and Hurricane Isaias approaching the northern Gulf Coast. The narrow checkpoint is 13:30-15:00 UTC, covering the cash open and the Michigan preliminary release.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a narrow overnight band as the Iran premium and long-end yields retrace
body: December NQ futures trade 31,051.25 on Yahoo Finance and 31,045.75 on Investing.com, up 0.26% and 0.25% from a 30,969.50 prior close, inside an overnight band of 30,953.00-31,089.75. That band spans 136.75 points, about 0.44%, and price holds its upper half while sitting 38-44 points below the high, so no session-extreme holding, no failed-retracement sequence and no repeated extension is observed. The advance partially retraces the prior session rather than extending it: the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed 30,725.81, down 434.27 points or 1.39%, after a 30,556.40-31,125.13 range from a 31,160.08 prior close. VIX settled 15.41, up 2.19% from 15.08, after fading an intraday 16.46 high to a 15.15 low, a low absolute level for a 1.39% index decline that indicates volatility decay rather than expansion. The driver of the decline remains a Financial Times report, since corroborated by Reuters, that OpenAI's September annualised revenue is near 50 billion dollars rather than the roughly 70 billion investors had inferred; the semiconductor gauge fell 3.4% and SoftBank fell as much as 7.3% to 5,600 yen in Tokyo on the same story before recovering to about 5,810 yen, down roughly 4%, while Nvidia is separately reported to be planning an investment in AI chip rival d-Matrix. Two amplifiers that were building earlier have now begun to decay. First, the long end has retraced: the 10-year yield closed 5.23%, down 5 basis points, after a 5.22-5.33% range, and the 30-year is near 5.61%, with Bloomberg describing Thursday's 30-year sale as solid; the H.15 release of 8 October shows the 2-year at 4.77% and the 10-year at 5.28% as of 7 October. Second, crude has reversed: Brent settled 104.11 dollars, up 3.9%, and WTI 91.18 dollars, up 3.3%, but both pared gains and now trade near 103.1 and 90.7, down about 1.1% and 0.8%, after President Trump said on Truth Social that the United States will not attack Iran before the 3 November midterm elections while the Hormuz blockade stays in force. That is a verified reduction in near-term geopolitical discontinuity risk rather than a resolution of the file. Hurricane Isaias remains the live energy variable: Reuters reports maximum sustained winds of 85 mph early Thursday with strengthening toward near Category 3 intensity and 110 mph forecast for Friday, landfall on the northern Gulf Coast late Friday into early Saturday, and increasing wind shear expected to limit intensity near landfall. About 63% of Gulf oil output, roughly 1.3 million barrels per day, is already shut in against 25% on Wednesday, personnel have been evacuated from 121 production platforms, and an Earth Science Associates model projects about 9 million barrels of lost output over the storm's duration. In Asia, the Nikkei trades 68,512.30, down 0.77% from a 69,042.11 close, having recovered from a 68,150.02 session low within a 68,689.74 high; that recovery is mean-reverting behaviour rather than one-way structure, and the Asia-versus-NQ divergence reduces directional conviction. Tail therefore eases into the lower half of the low band while the breadth of unresolved catalysts keeps Stress elevated. The shared Finviz context file was dated 29 September, roughly ten days old and marked partial with futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale and not used; this assessment rests on independently verified primary and reputable current sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held 10-14 through the Asian and early European hours of 8 October with Stress in the low 50s, stepped into the watch band at the 07:00 UTC handover and ran 20-23 through the European and early US session as the AI-led decline developed. The 17:00 UTC hour was the single elevated reading at Tail 28 with Stress 72 while the semiconductor drop was steepest. Tail then decayed to 16-18 from 20:00 UTC as the cash session recovered off its low and volatility failed to expand, with Confidence steady at 85-89 throughout.
outlookSummary: Tail eases to 16 in the current hour as the crude and long-end amplifiers retrace, holds there through the thin late-Asian hours, then rises gradually to the top of the low band into the 07:00 UTC European handover. It enters the watch band from 09:00 UTC on conditional range-expansion risk and peaks at 22 in the 14:00 UTC hour, which carries the Michigan preliminary release 30 minutes after the 13:30 UTC cash open. That 13:30-15:00 UTC window is the narrow checkpoint. Tail then eases through the US afternoon on a base case of volatility decay, lifts to 19 for the 20:00 UTC cash close and the scheduled Fed Collins speech, and drops to 12-13 once CME equity index futures reach their 21:00 UTC weekly halt, where no intraday path can form. Confidence declines from 88 to 80 across the horizon purely as a function of distance from the current observation set. Every forecast hour beyond the current one frames price-path structure conditionally.
